axes: glTF: +Y up. A Blender point (x, y, z) of film/blender is (x, z, -y) here. The desk top is the plane y = 0.

day.glow_what: emits: 1 = this thing is a light in this theme (the lamp from grey on, the tube in pink; the film's ring is plaster and never emits: raise it yourself on hover). strength: the mean scene-linear luminance its atlas texels hold (1.0 = display white), 0 when it does not emit: use it to drive bloom. The lit look itself is in the atlas.

atlas.how: TEXCOORD_1 of every mesh addresses its atlas (node extras.atlas, and the list here, say which of the two). The pictures hold display values (the film's Standard view): draw them unlit, as they are. They follow the glTF convention: load with flipY = false. Glass meshes have one point as their atlas UVs: they are drawn live.

day.aspect: 16:9 (fov_x is the film's; keep it and let fov_y follow on a wide screen)

grey.aspect: 16:9 (fov_x is the film's; keep it and let fov_y follow on a wide screen)

blue.aspect: 16:9 (fov_x is the film's; keep it and let fov_y follow on a wide screen)

pink.aspect: 16:9 (fov_x is the film's; keep it and let fov_y follow on a wide screen)

path.what: the film's camera, one sample per film frame (24 a second), f307 to f417

swing.what: the film's arc about the pivot, one value per path sample: azimuth = atan2(z, x) of (position - pivot) in degrees (90 = straight in front of the desk), elevation above the desk plane, distance in metres
swing.holes: the room has no wall behind the camera and no ceiling (the world colour shows there): keep the view within about 4 degrees of the path

mirror.what: the lacquer of the shot: 25 % pure mirror, a strong specular (F0 0.08) and a full clear coat. See review/P2/room3d/NOTES.md for the mix that reproduces the Cycles frame.
mirror.fit_what: measured at each theme's home camera, in linear light: Cycles desk = atlas x fit.atlas + mirror image x fit.mirror (mirror image = the room mirrored in the plane y = 0, blurred as roughness 0.11). Away from that view scale both by Fresnel.

desk.outline_what: [x, z] of the rim, anticlockwise seen from above in Blender; its back edge runs inside the round wall

wall.what: the round wall the desk hangs on: the table ends where a point is nearer than `radius` to `centre`

obj_projects.does: the laptop: click flies the camera into its screen; the lid answers (pivot_lid)

obj_ai.does: the ring: turns about its upright axis

obj_results.does: the vase: stem_blue and stem_pink lean and sway from their feet

obj_about.does: the chair: swivels about pivot_chair (upright) and turns back

obj_ball.does: the egg: can be pushed and rolls on the desk (node origin = its middle)

pivot_lid.what: the hinge line of the laptop: turn the node about its own X

pivot_fold.what: the fold in the lid (the screen pulls forward about its own X)

screen.what: one quad, UV 0..1 (u right, v up as the picture stands); the film's own picture is baked into the light atlas as the fallback

ball.table: desk.outline minus desk.wall; the other objects' place and radius are what it can bump into

env.what: equirectangular, display values, from the middle of the desk at laptop height. The middle column looks along +X, the picture turns toward +Z to the right, up is +Y: three.js EquirectangularReflectionMapping with no rotation. The laptop, vase, ring, card, glass, egg, books and papers are left out of it (the lamp, the desk and the room are in).
